LECTURE 17 Stage 3: Attention

Attention Variants & Optimizations

Making attention faster, cheaper, and more efficient for real-world LLMs
50 min read Hands-on coding Advanced

The O(n²) Problem

Standard self-attention has a fundamental limitation: its computational and memory costs grow quadratically with sequence length. For a sequence of length n, the attention matrix has n×n entries. This means:

  • 128 tokens: 16,384 attention entries — trivial
  • 2,048 tokens: ~4 million entries — manageable
  • 32,768 tokens: ~1 billion entries — challenging
  • 128,000 tokens (GPT-4 context): ~16 billion entries — requires optimization
  • 1M tokens (Gemini context): ~1 trillion entries — impossible with naive attention

This quadratic scaling is the single biggest bottleneck in scaling Transformers to long contexts. Every major advancement in LLM context length has required an attention optimization breakthrough.

Key Insight: The O(n²) cost comes from the fact that every token must compute an attention score with every other token. Reducing this cost requires either approximating attention (so not every pair is computed) or reorganizing the computation to be more memory-efficient (FlashAttention). These are fundamentally different strategies.

Flash Attention: Memory-Efficient Exact Attention

FlashAttention (Dao et al., 2022) does not approximate attention — it computes the exact same result as standard attention, but reorganizes the computation to minimize memory transfers between GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and on-chip SRAM (fast cache).

The key insight is that standard attention materializes the full n×n attention matrix in GPU memory, which is slow to read/write. FlashAttention instead:

  1. Tiles the computation: Breaks Q, K, V into blocks that fit in fast on-chip SRAM
  2. Fuses operations: Computes attention scores, softmax, and value weighting in one kernel, never writing the full attention matrix to slow HBM
  3. Uses online softmax: Computes softmax incrementally over blocks, maintaining running statistics

The result: 2-4x speedup and dramatically reduced memory usage. FlashAttention made training on long sequences practical and is now the default in most frameworks.

Important: FlashAttention is a CUDA kernel optimization — it cannot be fully replicated in pure Python/NumPy. We will study the algorithm conceptually and implement a simplified version to understand the tiling principle, but the real gains come from the GPU memory hierarchy optimization.

Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)

Grouped-Query Attention, introduced in the Llama 2 paper and used in most modern LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma), is an elegant compromise between Multi-Head Attention (MHA) and Multi-Query Attention (MQA).

The observation: during inference, the main memory bottleneck is storing the Key and Value tensors for all previous tokens (the KV-cache). With standard MHA, each head has its own K and V, so the cache grows as n_heads * seq_len * d_k * 2 (times 2 for K and V).

The GQA solution: Instead of giving every head its own K and V, group multiple query heads to share the same K and V heads:

  • MHA (standard): 32 Q heads, 32 K heads, 32 V heads — full memory cost
  • GQA (Llama 2 70B): 64 Q heads, 8 K heads, 8 V heads — 8x KV-cache reduction
  • MQA (extreme): 32 Q heads, 1 K head, 1 V head — 32x KV-cache reduction
Pro Tip: GQA was found to achieve nearly the same quality as MHA while being dramatically faster at inference. Llama 3 uses 8 KV heads with 32 Q heads (4:1 ratio). This has become the standard for open-weight models.

Multi-Query Attention (MQA)

Multi-Query Attention (Shazeer, 2019) is the extreme version of GQA where all query heads share a single set of keys and values. It was used in PaLM and several Google models.

MQA provides the maximum KV-cache savings but can degrade quality slightly, especially for smaller models. GQA was developed as a middle ground that retains most of MQA's speed benefits while recovering nearly all of MHA's quality.

Code: Implementing Grouped-Query Attention

Let us implement GQA from scratch. The key difference from standard MHA is that K and V have fewer heads, and we must broadcast (repeat) them to match the number of Q heads during the attention computation.

Python

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
 e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class GroupedQueryAttention:
 """Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) as used in Llama 2/3.

 n_q_heads query heads share n_kv_heads key/value heads.
 Each group of (n_q_heads // n_kv_heads) query heads shares one KV head.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, n_q_heads, n_kv_heads, seed=42):
 assert n_q_heads % n_kv_heads == 0, "n_q_heads must be divisible by n_kv_heads"

 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_q_heads = n_q_heads
 self.n_kv_heads = n_kv_heads
 self.n_groups = n_q_heads // n_kv_heads # queries per KV head
 self.d_k = d_model // n_q_heads

 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)

 # Q projection: full n_q_heads
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, n_q_heads * self.d_k) * scale
 # K, V projections: only n_kv_heads (smaller!)
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, n_kv_heads * self.d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, n_kv_heads * self.d_k) * scale
 # Output projection
 self.W_o = rng.randn(n_q_heads * self.d_k, d_model) * scale

 def forward(self, x, mask=None):
 batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape

 # Project
 Q = x @ self.W_q # (batch, seq, n_q_heads * d_k)
 K = x @ self.W_k # (batch, seq, n_kv_heads * d_k)
 V = x @ self.W_v # (batch, seq, n_kv_heads * d_k)

 # Reshape into heads
 Q = Q.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_q_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K = K.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_kv_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V = V.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_kv_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 # Q: (batch, n_q_heads, seq, d_k)
 # K: (batch, n_kv_heads, seq, d_k)

 # Repeat K, V to match Q head count
 # Each KV head is shared by n_groups query heads
 K = np.repeat(K, self.n_groups, axis=1) # (batch, n_q_heads, seq, d_k)
 V = np.repeat(V, self.n_groups, axis=1)

 # Standard attention from here
 scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
 if mask is not None:
 scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
 attn = softmax(scores)
 context = attn @ V

 # Merge heads
 context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, -1)
 return context @ self.W_o, attn

# Compare parameter counts: MHA vs GQA vs MQA
d_model = 256
n_q_heads = 8
seq_len = 16
batch_size = 1

print("=== Parameter Count Comparison ===")
print(f"d_model={d_model}, n_q_heads={n_q_heads}")
print()

configs = [
 ("MHA (8 KV heads)", 8),
 ("GQA (4 KV heads)", 4),
 ("GQA (2 KV heads)", 2),
 ("MQA (1 KV head)", 1),
]

np.random.seed(42)
x = np.random.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)
causal_mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1)

for name, n_kv in configs:
 gqa = GroupedQueryAttention(d_model, n_q_heads, n_kv, seed=42)

 q_params = gqa.W_q.size
 k_params = gqa.W_k.size
 v_params = gqa.W_v.size
 o_params = gqa.W_o.size
 total = q_params + k_params + v_params + o_params

 output, attn = gqa.forward(x, mask=causal_mask)

 kv_cache_size = 2 * n_kv * seq_len * (d_model // n_q_heads)

 print(f"{name}:")
 print(f" Q params: {q_params:>8,} K params: {k_params:>8,} "
 f"V params: {v_params:>8,} O params: {o_params:>8,}")
 print(f" Total params: {total:>8,} | KV-cache entries: {kv_cache_size:>6,} "
 f"| Output shape: {output.shape}")
 print()

print("Notice: GQA/MQA reduce K,V params and KV-cache size while keeping Q and O the same.")

KV-Cache for Inference Speedup

During autoregressive generation (producing one token at a time), recomputing attention over all previous tokens is wasteful. The KV-cache stores the Key and Value projections of previously generated tokens, so only the new token's Q, K, V need to be computed at each step.

Without KV-cache, generating N tokens requires O(N²) total attention operations (1 + 2 + 3 + ... + N). With KV-cache, each step is O(N), for a total of O(N²) as well, but with a much smaller constant factor since we avoid redundant K and V projections.

Code: KV-Cache Simulation

Python

import numpy as np
import time

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
 e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class AttentionWithKVCache:
 """Attention with KV-cache for efficient autoregressive generation."""

 def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_heads = n_heads
 self.d_k = d_model // n_heads

 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
 self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

 # KV cache: will grow as we generate tokens
 self.k_cache = None # (batch, n_heads, cached_len, d_k)
 self.v_cache = None

 def reset_cache(self):
 self.k_cache = None
 self.v_cache = None

 def forward_with_cache(self, x_new):
 """Process only the new token(s), using cached K,V for previous tokens.

 x_new: (batch, new_len, d_model) - typically new_len=1 during generation
 """
 batch, new_len, _ = x_new.shape

 # Only compute Q, K, V for new tokens
 Q_new = x_new @ self.W_q
 K_new = x_new @ self.W_k
 V_new = x_new @ self.W_v

 # Reshape into heads
 Q_new = Q_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K_new = K_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V_new = V_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

 # Append to cache
 if self.k_cache is None:
 self.k_cache = K_new
 self.v_cache = V_new
 else:
 self.k_cache = np.concatenate([self.k_cache, K_new], axis=2)
 self.v_cache = np.concatenate([self.v_cache, V_new], axis=2)

 # Attention: Q_new attends to ALL cached K, V
 scores = Q_new @ self.k_cache.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
 attn = softmax(scores)
 context = attn @ self.v_cache

 # Merge heads and project
 context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, new_len, self.d_model)
 return context @ self.W_o

 def forward_no_cache(self, x):
 """Standard forward pass without caching (for comparison)."""
 batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
 Q = (x @ self.W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K = (x @ self.W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V = (x @ self.W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

 # Apply causal mask
 mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1)
 scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
 scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
 attn = softmax(scores)
 context = (attn @ V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)
 return context @ self.W_o

# Simulate autoregressive generation with and without KV-cache
d_model = 64
n_heads = 4
gen_length = 20

np.random.seed(42)
# Simulate a prompt + generated tokens
all_tokens = np.random.randn(1, gen_length, d_model)

# Method 1: With KV-cache (generate one token at a time)
model_cached = AttentionWithKVCache(d_model, n_heads, seed=0)
model_cached.reset_cache()

print("=== Autoregressive Generation Comparison ===")
print(f"Generating {gen_length} tokens, d_model={d_model}, n_heads={n_heads}")
print()

cached_outputs = []
projection_ops_cached = 0
attention_ops_cached = 0

start = time.time()
for t in range(gen_length):
 token = all_tokens[:, t:t+1, :] # (1, 1, d_model)
 out = model_cached.forward_with_cache(token)
 cached_outputs.append(out)
 # Count operations: project 1 new token, attend to t+1 cached tokens
 projection_ops_cached += 3 * d_model * d_model # Q, K, V for 1 token
 attention_ops_cached += n_heads * 1 * (t+1) * (d_model // n_heads)
cached_time = (time.time() - start) * 1000

# Method 2: Without KV-cache (recompute everything each time)
model_no_cache = AttentionWithKVCache(d_model, n_heads, seed=0)
no_cache_outputs = []
projection_ops_no_cache = 0
attention_ops_no_cache = 0

start = time.time()
for t in range(gen_length):
 # Must recompute attention over ALL tokens so far
 context = all_tokens[:, :t+1, :] # (1, t+1, d_model)
 out = model_no_cache.forward_no_cache(context)
 no_cache_outputs.append(out[:, -1:, :]) # only need last token
 # Count: project all t+1 tokens, attend to (t+1)^2 pairs
 projection_ops_no_cache += 3 * (t+1) * d_model * d_model
 attention_ops_no_cache += n_heads * (t+1) * (t+1) * (d_model // n_heads)
no_cache_time = (time.time() - start) * 1000

# Verify outputs match
cached_final = np.concatenate(cached_outputs, axis=1)
no_cache_final = np.concatenate(no_cache_outputs, axis=1)

print(f"Results match: {np.allclose(cached_final, no_cache_final, atol=1e-6)}")
print()
print(f"With KV-cache: {cached_time:.2f} ms")
print(f"Without KV-cache: {no_cache_time:.2f} ms")
print(f"Speedup: {no_cache_time/cached_time:.1f}x")
print()
print(f"Projection operations - Cached: {projection_ops_cached:>12,} | No cache: {projection_ops_no_cache:>12,}")
print(f" Savings: {1 - projection_ops_cached/projection_ops_no_cache:.1%}")
print()
print(f"Attention operations - Cached: {attention_ops_cached:>12,} | No cache: {attention_ops_no_cache:>12,}")
print(f" Savings: {1 - attention_ops_cached/attention_ops_no_cache:.1%}")
print()
print(f"KV-cache size at end: {model_cached.k_cache.shape}")
print(f" = {model_cached.k_cache.size + model_cached.v_cache.size} float values stored")

Relative Position Encodings and RoPE

In the original Transformer, position information was added as absolute sinusoidal embeddings at the input. Modern LLMs have largely moved to Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), which encode position information directly into the attention computation.

The key idea behind RoPE: instead of adding position information to the input embeddings, rotate the Q and K vectors based on their positions. When two tokens at positions i and j compute their dot product, the rotation causes the score to depend on the relative distance (i - j) rather than the absolute positions.

Benefits of RoPE:

  • Relative by design: The model learns distance-based patterns, which generalize better
  • Length extrapolation: Can handle sequences longer than those seen during training (with techniques like NTK-aware scaling)
  • No extra parameters: The rotations are deterministic, not learned
  • Efficient: Applied as element-wise rotations, O(d) per token
Key Insight: RoPE is used in Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and most modern open-weight LLMs. It has become the de facto standard for position encoding, replacing both absolute sinusoidal and learned position embeddings.

Sliding Window Attention

Sliding Window Attention (used in Mistral, Mixtral, and Longformer) limits each token to only attend to a fixed window of nearby tokens, rather than the entire sequence. This reduces the O(n²) cost to O(n × w), where w is the window size.

Key properties:

  • Window size w: Mistral uses w=4096. Each token attends to the 4096 tokens before it.
  • Information propagation: With L layers and window size w, information can travel up to L×w tokens. With 32 layers and w=4096, that is 131,072 tokens of effective context.
  • Reduced KV-cache: Only w entries per head need to be cached, not the full sequence length.
Pro Tip: Sliding window attention is particularly effective when combined with a few "global" attention layers that see the full context. This hybrid approach (used in Longformer and BigBird) gets the best of both worlds: local patterns from window attention and global coherence from full attention.

Summary: Attention Variants at a Glance

Variant Complexity Used In Key Benefit
Standard MHA O(n²d) Original Transformer, BERT Full expressiveness
FlashAttention O(n²d) but IO-aware All modern training 2-4x speed, less memory
GQA O(n²d) Llama 2/3, Mistral Smaller KV-cache
MQA O(n²d) PaLM, Falcon Minimum KV-cache
Sliding Window O(n·w·d) Mistral, Longformer Linear in seq length

Key Takeaways

  • Standard attention scales as O(n²) in both computation and memory, making long-context LLMs challenging without optimization.
  • FlashAttention computes exact attention but reorganizes memory access patterns for 2-4x GPU speedup — it is now the default for training.
  • Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) shares K/V heads across groups of Q heads, dramatically reducing the KV-cache size during inference with minimal quality loss.
  • KV-caching avoids recomputing Key and Value projections for previously generated tokens, providing significant speedup for autoregressive generation.
  • RoPE encodes relative position information through vector rotations, enabling better length generalization than absolute position embeddings.
  • Sliding window attention limits each token to a local context window, reducing complexity from O(n²) to O(n·w) at the cost of direct long-range access in a single layer.

LECȚIA 17 Etapa 3: Atenție

Variante și optimizări ale atenției

Cum facem atenția mai rapidă, mai ieftină și mai eficientă pentru LLM-uri reale
50 min lectură Programare practică Avansat

Problema O(n²)

Auto-atenția standard are o limitare fundamentală: costurile sale de calcul și memorie cresc pătratic cu lungimea secvenței. Pentru o secvență de lungime n, matricea de atenție are n×n intrări. Aceasta înseamnă:

  • 128 tokeni: 16.384 intrări de atenție — trivial
  • 2.048 tokeni: ~4 milioane intrări — gestionabil
  • 32.768 tokeni: ~1 miliard intrări — provocator
  • 128.000 tokeni (contextul GPT-4): ~16 miliarde intrări — necesită optimizare
  • 1M tokeni (contextul Gemini): ~1 trilion intrări — imposibil cu atenție naivă

Această scalare pătratică este cel mai mare blocaj în scalarea Transformerelor la contexte lungi. Fiecare avans major în lungimea contextului LLM a necesitat o descoperire în optimizarea atenției.

Observație cheie: Costul O(n²) provine din faptul că fiecare token trebuie să calculeze un scor de atenție cu fiecare alt token. Reducerea acestui cost necesită fie aproximarea atenției (astfel încât nu fiecare pereche este calculată), fie reorganizarea calculului pentru a fi mai eficientă din punct de vedere al memoriei (FlashAttention). Acestea sunt strategii fundamental diferite.

Flash Attention: Atenție exactă eficientă din punct de vedere al memoriei

FlashAttention (Dao et al., 2022) nu aproximează atenția — calculează exact același rezultat ca atenția standard, dar reorganizează calculul pentru a minimiza transferurile de memorie între memoria de bandă mare a GPU-ului (HBM) și SRAM-ul on-chip (cache rapid).

Observația cheie este că atenția standard materializează matricea completă de atenție n×n în memoria GPU, ceea ce este lent de citit/scris. FlashAttention în schimb:

  1. Împarte calculul în blocuri: Fragmentează Q, K, V în blocuri care încap în SRAM-ul rapid on-chip
  2. Fuzionează operațiile: Calculează scorurile de atenție, softmax și ponderarea valorilor într-un singur kernel, fără a scrie vreodată matricea completă de atenție în HBM-ul lent
  3. Folosește softmax online: Calculează softmax incremental pe blocuri, menținând statistici curente

Rezultatul: accelerare de 2-4x și utilizare dramatic redusă a memoriei. FlashAttention a făcut antrenamentul pe secvențe lungi practic și este acum implicit în majoritatea framework-urilor.

Important: FlashAttention este o optimizare de kernel CUDA — nu poate fi replicată complet în Python/NumPy pur. Vom studia algoritmul conceptual și vom implementa o versiune simplificată pentru a înțelege principiul de împărțire în blocuri, dar câștigurile reale provin din optimizarea ierarhiei de memorie a GPU-ului.

Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)

Grouped-Query Attention, introdusă în lucrarea Llama 2 și folosită în cele mai multe LLM-uri moderne (Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma), este un compromis elegant între Multi-Head Attention (MHA) și Multi-Query Attention (MQA).

Observația: în timpul inferenței, principalul blocaj de memorie este stocarea tensorilor Key și Value pentru toți tokenii anteriori (KV-cache). Cu MHA standard, fiecare cap are propriii K și V, astfel încât cache-ul crește ca n_heads * seq_len * d_k * 2 (ori 2 pentru K și V).

Soluția GQA: În loc să dăm fiecărui cap propriii K și V, grupăm mai multe capete de query pentru a partaja aceleași capete K și V:

  • MHA (standard): 32 capete Q, 32 capete K, 32 capete V — cost complet de memorie
  • GQA (Llama 2 70B): 64 capete Q, 8 capete K, 8 capete V — reducere de 8x a KV-cache
  • MQA (extrem): 32 capete Q, 1 cap K, 1 cap V — reducere de 32x a KV-cache

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
 e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class GroupedQueryAttention:
 """Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) as used in Llama 2/3.

 n_q_heads query heads share n_kv_heads key/value heads.
 Each group of (n_q_heads // n_kv_heads) query heads shares one KV head.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, n_q_heads, n_kv_heads, seed=42):
 assert n_q_heads % n_kv_heads == 0, "n_q_heads must be divisible by n_kv_heads"

 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_q_heads = n_q_heads
 self.n_kv_heads = n_kv_heads
 self.n_groups = n_q_heads // n_kv_heads # queries per KV head
 self.d_k = d_model // n_q_heads

 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)

 # Q projection: full n_q_heads
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, n_q_heads * self.d_k) * scale
 # K, V projections: only n_kv_heads (smaller!)
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, n_kv_heads * self.d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, n_kv_heads * self.d_k) * scale
 # Output projection
 self.W_o = rng.randn(n_q_heads * self.d_k, d_model) * scale

 def forward(self, x, mask=None):
 batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape

 # Project
 Q = x @ self.W_q # (batch, seq, n_q_heads * d_k)
 K = x @ self.W_k # (batch, seq, n_kv_heads * d_k)
 V = x @ self.W_v # (batch, seq, n_kv_heads * d_k)

 # Reshape into heads
 Q = Q.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_q_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K = K.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_kv_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V = V.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_kv_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 # Q: (batch, n_q_heads, seq, d_k)
 # K: (batch, n_kv_heads, seq, d_k)

 # Repeat K, V to match Q head count
 # Each KV head is shared by n_groups query heads
 K = np.repeat(K, self.n_groups, axis=1) # (batch, n_q_heads, seq, d_k)
 V = np.repeat(V, self.n_groups, axis=1)

 # Standard attention from here
 scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
 if mask is not None:
 scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
 attn = softmax(scores)
 context = attn @ V

 # Merge heads
 context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, -1)
 return context @ self.W_o, attn

KV-Cache pentru accelerarea inferenței

În timpul generării autoregresive (producând un token la un moment dat), recalcularea atenției peste toți tokenii anteriori este ineficientă. KV-cache stochează proiecțiile Key și Value ale tokenilor generați anterior, astfel încât doar Q, K, V ale noului token trebuie calculate la fiecare pas.

Fără KV-cache, generarea a N tokeni necesită O(N²) operații totale de atenție (1 + 2 + 3 + ... + N). Cu KV-cache, fiecare pas este O(N), pentru un total de O(N²) de asemenea, dar cu un factor constant mult mai mic deoarece evităm proiecțiile redundante K și V.

Cod: Simularea KV-Cache

import numpy as np
import time

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
 e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class AttentionWithKVCache:
 """Attention with KV-cache for efficient autoregressive generation."""

 def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_heads = n_heads
 self.d_k = d_model // n_heads

 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
 self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

 # KV cache: will grow as we generate tokens
 self.k_cache = None # (batch, n_heads, cached_len, d_k)
 self.v_cache = None

 def reset_cache(self):
 self.k_cache = None
 self.v_cache = None

 def forward_with_cache(self, x_new):
 """Process only the new token(s), using cached K,V for previous tokens.

 x_new: (batch, new_len, d_model) - typically new_len=1 during generation
 """
 batch, new_len, _ = x_new.shape

 # Only compute Q, K, V for new tokens
 Q_new = x_new @ self.W_q
 K_new = x_new @ self.W_k
 V_new = x_new @ self.W_v

 # Reshape into heads
 Q_new = Q_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K_new = K_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V_new = V_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

 # Append to cache
 if self.k_cache is None:
 self.k_cache = K_new
 self.v_cache = V_new
 else:
 self.k_cache = np.concatenate([self.k_cache, K_new], axis=2)
 self.v_cache = np.concatenate([self.v_cache, V_new], axis=2)

 # Attention: Q_new attends to ALL cached K, V
 scores = Q_new @ self.k_cache.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
 attn = softmax(scores)
 context = attn @ self.v_cache

 # Merge heads and project
 context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, new_len, self.d_model)
 return context @ self.W_o

 def forward_no_cache(self, x):
 """Standard forward pass without caching (for comparison)."""
 batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
 Q = (x @ self.W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K = (x @ self.W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V = (x @ self.W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

 # Apply causal mask
 mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1)
 scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
 scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
 attn = softmax(scores)
 context = (attn @ V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)
 return context @ self.W_o

# Simulate autoregressive generation with and without KV-cache
d_model = 64
n_heads = 4
gen_length = 20

np.random.seed(42)
# Simulate a prompt + generated tokens
all_tokens = np.random.randn(1, gen_length, d_model)

# Method 1: With KV-cache (generate one token at a time)
model_cached = AttentionWithKVCache(d_model, n_heads, seed=0)
model_cached.reset_cache()

print("=== Autoregressive Generation Comparison ===")
print(f"Generating {gen_length} tokens, d_model={d_model}, n_heads={n_heads}")
print()

cached_outputs = []
projection_ops_cached = 0
attention_ops_cached = 0

start = time.time()
for t in range(gen_length):
 token = all_tokens[:, t:t+1, :] # (1, 1, d_model)
 out = model_cached.forward_with_cache(token)
 cached_outputs.append(out)

cached_time = (time.time() - start) * 1000

# Method 2: Without KV-cache (recompute everything each time)
model_no_cache = AttentionWithKVCache(d_model, n_heads, seed=0)
no_cache_outputs = []
projection_ops_no_cache = 0
attention_ops_no_cache = 0

start = time.time()

 # Count: project all t+1 tokens, attend to (t+1)^2 pairs
 projection_ops_no_cache += 3 * (t+1) * d_model * d_model
 attention_ops_no_cache += n_heads * (t+1) * (t+1) * (d_model // n_heads)
no_cache_time = (time.time() - start) * 1000

# Verify outputs match
cached_final = np.concatenate(cached_outputs, axis=1)
no_cache_final = np.concatenate(no_cache_outputs, axis=1)

print()

print(f"Without KV-cache: {no_cache_time:.2f} ms")

print(f" Savings: {1 - projection_ops_cached/projection_ops_no_cache:.1%}")

Codificări poziționale relative și RoPE

În Transformerul original, informația despre poziție era adăugată ca embedding-uri sinusoidale absolute la intrare. LLM-urile moderne au trecut în mare parte la Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), care codifică informația despre poziție direct în calculul de atenție.

Ideea cheie din spatele RoPE: în loc de a adăuga informația despre poziție la embedding-urile de intrare, rotim vectorii Q și K în funcție de pozițiile lor. Când doi tokeni la pozițiile i și j calculează produsul lor scalar, rotația face ca scorul să depindă de distanța relativă (i - j) mai degrabă decât de pozițiile absolute.

Beneficiile RoPE:

  • Relativ prin design: Modelul învață tipare bazate pe distanță, care se generalizează mai bine
  • Extrapolare a lungimii: Poate gestiona secvențe mai lungi decât cele văzute în timpul antrenamentului (cu tehnici precum scalarea NTK-aware)
  • Fără parametri suplimentari: Rotațiile sunt deterministe, nu învățate
  • Eficient: Aplicat ca rotații element cu element, O(d) per token
Observație cheie: RoPE este folosit în Llama, Mistral, Gemma și cele mai multe LLM-uri moderne cu ponderi deschise. A devenit standardul de facto pentru codificarea pozițională, înlocuind atât embedding-urile sinusoidale absolute cât și cele poziționale învățate.

Atenție cu fereastră glisantă

Atenția cu fereastră glisantă (folosită în Mistral, Mixtral și Longformer) limitează fiecare token să acorde atenție doar unei ferestre fixe de tokeni apropiați, în loc de întreaga secvență. Aceasta reduce costul O(n²) la O(n × w), unde w este dimensiunea ferestrei.

Proprietăți cheie:

  • Dimensiunea ferestrei w: Mistral folosește w=4096. Fiecare token acordă atenție celor 4096 tokeni dinaintea sa.
  • Propagarea informației: Cu L straturi și dimensiunea ferestrei w, informația poate călători până la L×w tokeni. Cu 32 de straturi și w=4096, aceasta înseamnă 131.072 tokeni de context efectiv.
  • KV-cache redus: Doar w intrări per cap trebuie stocate în cache, nu întreaga lungime a secvenței.
Sfat profesional: Atenția cu fereastră glisantă este deosebit de eficientă atunci când este combinată cu câteva straturi de atenție „globale" care văd întregul context. Această abordare hibridă (folosită în Longformer și BigBird) obține ce e mai bun din ambele lumi: tipare locale din atenția cu fereastră și coerență globală din atenția completă.

Rezumat: Variante de atenție pe scurt

Variantă Complexitate Folosit în Beneficiu cheie
MHA standard O(n²d) Transformer original, BERT Expresivitate completă
FlashAttention O(n²d) dar IO-aware Tot antrenamentul modern Viteză 2-4x, mai puțină memorie
GQA O(n²d) Llama 2/3, Mistral KV-cache mai mic
MQA O(n²d) PaLM, Falcon KV-cache minim
Fereastră glisantă O(n·w·d) Mistral, Longformer Liniar în lungimea secvenței

Concluzii cheie

  • Atenția standard scalează ca O(n²) atât în calcul cât și în memorie, făcând LLM-urile cu context lung provocatoare fără optimizare.
  • FlashAttention calculează atenția exactă dar reorganizează tiparele de acces la memorie pentru o accelerare de 2-4x pe GPU — este acum implicit pentru antrenament.
  • Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) partajează capetele K/V între grupuri de capete Q, reducând dramatic dimensiunea KV-cache în timpul inferenței cu pierderi minime de calitate.
  • KV-caching evită recalcularea proiecțiilor Key și Value pentru tokenii generați anterior, oferind o accelerare semnificativă pentru generarea autoregresivă.
  • RoPE codifică informația pozițională relativă prin rotații de vectori, permițând o generalizare mai bună a lungimii decât embedding-urile poziționale absolute.
  • Atenția cu fereastră glisantă limitează fiecare token la o fereastră de context local, reducând complexitatea de la O(n²) la O(n·w) cu prețul accesului direct la distanțe lungi într-un singur strat.

  3. Χρησιμοποιει online softmax: Υπολογιζει το softmax σταδιακα σε μπλοκ, διατηρωντας τρεχουσα στατιστικα

Το αποτελεσμα: 2-4x επιταχυνση και δραματικα μειωμενη χρηση μνημης. Το FlashAttention κατεστησε πρακτικη την εκπαιδευση σε μεγαλες ακολουθιες και ειναι πλεον το προεπιλεγμενο στα περισσοτερα frameworks.

Σημαντικο: Το FlashAttention ειναι μια βελτιστοποιηση CUDA kernel — δεν μπορει να αναπαραχθει πληρως σε καθαρη Python/NumPy. Θα μελετησουμε τον αλγοριθμο εννοιολογικα και θα υλοποιησουμε μια απλοποιημενη εκδοχη για να κατανοησουμε την αρχη του tiling, αλλα τα πραγματικα οφελη προερχονται απο τη βελτιστοποιηση της ιεραρχιας μνημης της GPU.

Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)

Το Grouped-Query Attention, που παρουσιαστηκε στο αρθρο του Llama 2 και χρησιμοποιειται στα περισσοτερα συγχρονα LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma), ειναι ενας κομψος συμβιβασμος μεταξυ MHA και MQA.

Η παρατηρηση: κατα τη διαδικασια εξαγωγης συμπερασματων (inference), το κυριο εμποδιο μνημης ειναι η αποθηκευση των τανυστων Key και Value για ολα τα προηγουμενα tokens (το KV-cache). Με κανονικο MHA, καθε head εχει τα δικα του K και V, οποτε η κρυφη μνημη αυξανεται ως n_heads * seq_len * d_k * 2 (επι 2 για K και V).

Η λυση GQA: Αντι να δινει σε καθε head τα δικα του K και V, ομαδοποιει πολλαπλα query heads για να μοιραζονται τα ιδια K και V heads:

  • MHA (κανονικο): 32 Q heads, 32 K heads, 32 V heads — πληρες κοστος μνημης
  • GQA (Llama 2 70B): 64 Q heads, 8 K heads, 8 V heads — 8x μειωση KV-cache
  • MQA (ακραιο): 32 Q heads, 1 K head, 1 V head — 32x μειωση KV-cache
Συμβουλη: Το GQA βρεθηκε να επιτυγχανει σχεδον την ιδια ποιοτητα με το MHA, ενω ειναι δραματικα πιο γρηγορο στο inference. Το Llama 3 χρησιμοποιει 8 KV heads με 32 Q heads (αναλογια 4:1). Αυτο εχει γινει το προτυπο για μοντελα ανοιχτων βαρων.

Multi-Query Attention (MQA)

Το Multi-Query Attention (Shazeer, 2019) ειναι η ακραια εκδοχη του GQA οπου ολα τα query heads μοιραζονται ενα μοναδικο σετ keys και values. Χρησιμοποιηθηκε στο PaLM και σε αρκετα μοντελα της Google.

Το MQA παρεχει τη μεγιστη εξοικονομηση KV-cache αλλα μπορει να υποβαθμισει ελαφρως την ποιοτητα, ειδικα για μικροτερα μοντελα. Το GQA αναπτυχθηκε ως μεσαια λυση που διατηρει τα περισσοτερα οφελη ταχυτητας του MQA ενω ανακτα σχεδον ολη την ποιοτητα του MHA.

Ας υλοποιησουμε το GQA απο την αρχη. Η βασικη διαφορα απο το κανονικο MHA ειναι οτι τα K και V εχουν λιγοτερα heads, και πρεπει να τα εκπεμψουμε (broadcast/repeat) για να ταιριαζουν με τον αριθμο των Q heads κατα τον υπολογισμο attention.

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
 e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class GroupedQueryAttention:
 """Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) as used in Llama 2/3.

 n_q_heads query heads share n_kv_heads key/value heads.
 Each group of (n_q_heads // n_kv_heads) query heads shares one KV head.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, n_q_heads, n_kv_heads, seed=42):
 assert n_q_heads % n_kv_heads == 0, "n_q_heads must be divisible by n_kv_heads"

 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_q_heads = n_q_heads
 self.n_kv_heads = n_kv_heads
 self.n_groups = n_q_heads // n_kv_heads # queries per KV head
 self.d_k = d_model // n_q_heads

 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)

 # Q projection: full n_q_heads
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, n_q_heads * self.d_k) * scale
 # K, V projections: only n_kv_heads (smaller!)
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, n_kv_heads * self.d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, n_kv_heads * self.d_k) * scale
 # Output projection
 self.W_o = rng.randn(n_q_heads * self.d_k, d_model) * scale

 def forward(self, x, mask=None):
 batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape

 # Project
 Q = x @ self.W_q # (batch, seq, n_q_heads * d_k)
 K = x @ self.W_k # (batch, seq, n_kv_heads * d_k)
 V = x @ self.W_v # (batch, seq, n_kv_heads * d_k)

 # Reshape into heads
 Q = Q.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_q_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K = K.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_kv_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V = V.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_kv_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 # Q: (batch, n_q_heads, seq, d_k)
 # K: (batch, n_kv_heads, seq, d_k)

 # Repeat K, V to match Q head count
 # Each KV head is shared by n_groups query heads
 K = np.repeat(K, self.n_groups, axis=1) # (batch, n_q_heads, seq, d_k)
 V = np.repeat(V, self.n_groups, axis=1)

 # Standard attention from here
 scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
 if mask is not None:
 scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
 attn = softmax(scores)
 context = attn @ V

 # Merge heads
 context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, -1)
 return context @ self.W_o, attn

KV-Cache για Επιταχυνση στο Inference

Κατα την αυτοπαλινδρομικη παραγωγη (παραγωγη ενος token καθε φορα), ο επαναυπολογισμος του attention για ολα τα προηγουμενα tokens ειναι σπαταλη. Το KV-cache αποθηκευει τις προβολες Key και Value των προηγουμενων tokens, ωστε μονο τα Q, K, V του νεου token να χρειαζονται υπολογισμο σε καθε βημα.

Χωρις KV-cache, η παραγωγη N tokens απαιτει O(N²) συνολικες λειτουργιες attention (1 + 2 + 3 + ... + N). Με KV-cache, καθε βημα ειναι O(N), για συνολο O(N²) επισης, αλλα με πολυ μικροτερο σταθερο παραγοντα καθως αποφευγουμε περιττες προβολες K και V.

Κωδικας: Προσομοιωση KV-Cache

Python

import numpy as np
import time

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
 e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class AttentionWithKVCache:
 """Attention with KV-cache for efficient autoregressive generation."""

 def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
 self.d_model = d_model
 self.n_heads = n_heads
 self.d_k = d_model // n_heads

 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
 self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

 # KV cache: will grow as we generate tokens
 self.k_cache = None # (batch, n_heads, cached_len, d_k)
 self.v_cache = None

 def reset_cache(self):
 self.k_cache = None
 self.v_cache = None

 def forward_with_cache(self, x_new):
 """Process only the new token(s), using cached K,V for previous tokens.

 x_new: (batch, new_len, d_model) - typically new_len=1 during generation
 """
 batch, new_len, _ = x_new.shape

 # Only compute Q, K, V for new tokens
 Q_new = x_new @ self.W_q
 K_new = x_new @ self.W_k
 V_new = x_new @ self.W_v

 # Reshape into heads
 Q_new = Q_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K_new = K_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V_new = V_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

 # Append to cache
 if self.k_cache is None:
 self.k_cache = K_new
 self.v_cache = V_new
 else:
 self.k_cache = np.concatenate([self.k_cache, K_new], axis=2)
 self.v_cache = np.concatenate([self.v_cache, V_new], axis=2)

 # Attention: Q_new attends to ALL cached K, V
 scores = Q_new @ self.k_cache.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
 attn = softmax(scores)
 context = attn @ self.v_cache

 # Merge heads and project
 context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, new_len, self.d_model)
 return context @ self.W_o

 def forward_no_cache(self, x):
 """Standard forward pass without caching (for comparison)."""
 batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
 Q = (x @ self.W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 K = (x @ self.W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
 V = (x @ self.W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

 # Apply causal mask
 mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1)
 scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
 scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
 attn = softmax(scores)
 context = (attn @ V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)
 return context @ self.W_o

Σχετικη Κωδικοποιηση Θεσης και RoPE

Στον αρχικο Transformer, η πληροφορια θεσης προστιθεται ως απολυτα ημιτονοειδη embeddings στην εισοδο. Τα συγχρονα LLMs εχουν σε μεγαλο βαθμο μεταβει στα Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), που κωδικοποιουν την πληροφορια θεσης απευθειας στον υπολογισμο attention.

Η βασικη ιδεα πισω απο το RoPE: αντι να προσθετουμε πληροφορια θεσης στα embeddings εισοδου, περιστρεφουμε τα διανυσματα Q και K με βαση τις θεσεις τους. Οταν δυο tokens στις θεσεις i και j υπολογιζουν το εσωτερικο γινομενο τους, η περιστροφη κανει το σκορ να εξαρταται απο τη σχετικη αποσταση (i - j) αντι απο τις απολυτες θεσεις.

Πλεονεκτηματα του RoPE:

  • Σχετικο απο σχεδιασμο: Το μοντελο μαθαινει μοτιβα βασισμενα στην αποσταση, που γενικευονται καλυτερα
  • Επεκταση μηκους: Μπορει να χειριστει ακολουθιες μεγαλυτερες απο αυτες που ειδε κατα την εκπαιδευση (με τεχνικες οπως NTK-aware scaling)
  • Χωρις επιπλεον παραμετρους: Οι περιστροφες ειναι ντετερμινιστικες, οχι εκπαιδευσιμες
  • Αποδοτικο: Εφαρμοζονται ως περιστροφες κατα στοιχειο, O(d) ανα token
Βασικη Ιδεα: Το RoPE χρησιμοποιειται στα Llama, Mistral, Gemma και στα περισσοτερα συγχρονα LLMs ανοιχτων βαρων. Εχει γινει το de facto προτυπο για κωδικοποιηση θεσης, αντικαθιστωντας τοσο τα απολυτα ημιτονοειδη οσο και τα εκπαιδευσιμα embeddings θεσης.

Sliding Window Attention

Το Sliding Window Attention (που χρησιμοποιειται στα Mistral, Mixtral και Longformer) περιοριζει καθε token να προσεχει μονο σε ενα σταθερο παραθυρο κοντινων tokens, αντι σε ολοκληρη την ακολουθια. Αυτο μειωνει το κοστος O(n²) σε O(n × w), οπου w ειναι το μεγεθος του παραθυρου.

Βασικες ιδιοτητες:

  • Μεγεθος παραθυρου w: Το Mistral χρησιμοποιει w=4096. Καθε token προσεχει στα 4096 tokens πριν απο αυτο.
  • Διαδοση πληροφοριας: Με L επιπεδα και μεγεθος παραθυρου w, η πληροφορια μπορει να ταξιδεψει εως L×w tokens. Με 32 επιπεδα και w=4096, αυτο ειναι 131.072 tokens ενεργου πλαισιου.
  • Μειωμενο KV-cache: Μονο w καταχωρησεις ανα head χρειαζονται στην κρυφη μνημη, οχι ολοκληρο το μηκος της ακολουθιας.
Συμβουλη: Το sliding window attention ειναι ιδιαιτερα αποτελεσματικο οταν συνδυαζεται με μερικα "ολικα" επιπεδα attention που βλεπουν ολοκληρο το πλαισιο. Αυτη η υβριδικη προσεγγιση (που χρησιμοποιειται στο Longformer και το BigBird) προσφερει το καλυτερο και απο τους δυο κοσμους: τοπικα μοτιβα απο το window attention και συνολικη συνοχη απο το πληρες attention.

  • Το κανονικο attention κλιμακωνεται ως O(n²) τοσο σε υπολογισμο οσο και σε μνημη, καθιστωντας τα LLMs μεγαλου πλαισιου προκλητικα χωρις βελτιστοποιηση.
  • Το FlashAttention υπολογιζει ακριβες attention αλλα αναδιοργανωνει τα μοτιβα προσβασης μνημης για 2-4x επιταχυνση GPU — ειναι πλεον το προεπιλεγμενο για εκπαιδευση.
  • Το Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) μοιραζει K/V heads σε ομαδες Q heads, μειωνοντας δραματικα το μεγεθος του KV-cache κατα το inference με ελαχιστη απωλεια ποιοτητας.
  • Το KV-caching αποφευγει τον επαναυπολογισμο των προβολων Key και Value για προηγουμενα tokens, προσφεροντας σημαντικη επιταχυνση για την αυτοπαλινδρομικη παραγωγη.
  • Το RoPE κωδικοποιει σχετικη πληροφορια θεσης μεσω περιστροφων διανυσματων, επιτρεποντας καλυτερη γενικευση μηκους απο τα απολυτα embeddings θεσης.
  • Το sliding window attention περιοριζει καθε token σε ενα τοπικο παραθυρο πλαισιου, μειωνοντας την πολυπλοκοτητα απο O(n²) σε O(n·w) με κοστος την αμεση προσβαση μεγαλης εμβελειας σε ενα μονο επιπεδο.

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
    x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class GroupedQueryAttention:
    """Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) as used in Llama 2/3.

    n_q_heads query heads share n_kv_heads key/value heads.
    Each group of (n_q_heads // n_kv_heads) query heads shares one KV head.
    """

    def __init__(self, d_model, n_q_heads, n_kv_heads, seed=42):
        assert n_q_heads % n_kv_heads == 0, "n_q_heads must be divisible by n_kv_heads"

        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_q_heads = n_q_heads
        self.n_kv_heads = n_kv_heads
        self.n_groups = n_q_heads // n_kv_heads  # queries per KV head
        self.d_k = d_model // n_q_heads

        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)

        # Q projection: full n_q_heads
        self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, n_q_heads * self.d_k) * scale
        # K, V projections: only n_kv_heads (smaller!)
        self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, n_kv_heads * self.d_k) * scale
        self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, n_kv_heads * self.d_k) * scale
        # Output projection
        self.W_o = rng.randn(n_q_heads * self.d_k, d_model) * scale

    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape

        # Project
        Q = x @ self.W_q  # (batch, seq, n_q_heads * d_k)
        K = x @ self.W_k  # (batch, seq, n_kv_heads * d_k)
        V = x @ self.W_v  # (batch, seq, n_kv_heads * d_k)

        # Reshape into heads
        Q = Q.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_q_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        K = K.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_kv_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        V = V.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_kv_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        # Q: (batch, n_q_heads, seq, d_k)
        # K: (batch, n_kv_heads, seq, d_k)

        # Repeat K, V to match Q head count
        # Each KV head is shared by n_groups query heads
        K = np.repeat(K, self.n_groups, axis=1)  # (batch, n_q_heads, seq, d_k)
        V = np.repeat(V, self.n_groups, axis=1)

        # Standard attention from here
        scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
        attn = softmax(scores)
        context = attn @ V

        # Merge heads
        context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, -1)
        return context @ self.W_o, attn

# Compare parameter counts: MHA vs GQA vs MQA

n_q_heads = 8
seq_len = 16

    ("GQA (4 KV heads)", 4),
    ("GQA (2 KV heads)", 2),
    ("MQA (1 KV head)", 1),
]

np.random.seed(42)
x = np.random.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)
causal_mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1)

for name, n_kv in configs:
    gqa = GroupedQueryAttention(d_model, n_q_heads, n_kv, seed=42)

    q_params = gqa.W_q.size
    k_params = gqa.W_k.size
    v_params = gqa.W_v.size
    o_params = gqa.W_o.size
    total = q_params + k_params + v_params + o_params

    output, attn = gqa.forward(x, mask=causal_mask)

    kv_cache_size = 2 * n_kv * seq_len * (d_model // n_q_heads)

    print(f"{name}:")
    print(f"  Q params: {q_params:>8,}  K params: {k_params:>8,}  "
          f"V params: {v_params:>8,}  O params: {o_params:>8,}")
    print(f"  Total params: {total:>8,}  |  KV-cache entries: {kv_cache_size:>6,}  "
          f"|  Output shape: {output.shape}")
    print()

print("Notice: GQA/MQA reduce K,V params and KV-cache size while keeping Q and O the same.")

import numpy as np
import time

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
    x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class AttentionWithKVCache:
    """Attention with KV-cache for efficient autoregressive generation."""

    def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // n_heads

        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)
        self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

        # KV cache: will grow as we generate tokens
        self.k_cache = None  # (batch, n_heads, cached_len, d_k)
        self.v_cache = None

    def reset_cache(self):
        self.k_cache = None
        self.v_cache = None

    def forward_with_cache(self, x_new):
        """Process only the new token(s), using cached K,V for previous tokens.

        x_new: (batch, new_len, d_model) - typically new_len=1 during generation
        """
        batch, new_len, _ = x_new.shape

        # Only compute Q, K, V for new tokens
        Q_new = x_new @ self.W_q
        K_new = x_new @ self.W_k
        V_new = x_new @ self.W_v

        # Reshape into heads
        Q_new = Q_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        K_new = K_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        V_new = V_new.reshape(batch, new_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

        # Append to cache
        if self.k_cache is None:
            self.k_cache = K_new
            self.v_cache = V_new
        else:
            self.k_cache = np.concatenate([self.k_cache, K_new], axis=2)
            self.v_cache = np.concatenate([self.v_cache, V_new], axis=2)

        # Attention: Q_new attends to ALL cached K, V
        scores = Q_new @ self.k_cache.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        attn = softmax(scores)
        context = attn @ self.v_cache

        # Merge heads and project
        context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, new_len, self.d_model)
        return context @ self.W_o

    def forward_no_cache(self, x):
        """Standard forward pass without caching (for comparison)."""
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        Q = (x @ self.W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        K = (x @ self.W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        V = (x @ self.W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

        # Apply causal mask
        mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1)
        scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
        attn = softmax(scores)
        context = (attn @ V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)
        return context @ self.W_o

# Simulate autoregressive generation with and without KV-cache
d_model = 64
n_heads = 4
gen_length = 20

np.random.seed(42)
# Simulate a prompt + generated tokens
all_tokens = np.random.randn(1, gen_length, d_model)

# Method 1: With KV-cache (generate one token at a time)
model_cached = AttentionWithKVCache(d_model, n_heads, seed=0)
model_cached.reset_cache()

print("=== Autoregressive Generation Comparison ===")
print(f"Generating {gen_length} tokens, d_model={d_model}, n_heads={n_heads}")
print()

cached_outputs = []
projection_ops_cached = 0
attention_ops_cached = 0

start = time.time()
for t in range(gen_length):
    token = all_tokens[:, t:t+1, :]  # (1, 1, d_model)
    out = model_cached.forward_with_cache(token)
    cached_outputs.append(out)
    # Count operations: project 1 new token, attend to t+1 cached tokens
    projection_ops_cached += 3 * d_model * d_model  # Q, K, V for 1 token
    attention_ops_cached += n_heads * 1 * (t+1) * (d_model // n_heads)
cached_time = (time.time() - start) * 1000

# Method 2: Without KV-cache (recompute everything each time)
model_no_cache = AttentionWithKVCache(d_model, n_heads, seed=0)
no_cache_outputs = []
projection_ops_no_cache = 0
attention_ops_no_cache = 0

start = time.time()
for t in range(gen_length):
    # Must recompute attention over ALL tokens so far
    context = all_tokens[:, :t+1, :]  # (1, t+1, d_model)
    out = model_no_cache.forward_no_cache(context)
    no_cache_outputs.append(out[:, -1:, :])  # only need last token
    # Count: project all t+1 tokens, attend to (t+1)^2 pairs
    projection_ops_no_cache += 3 * (t+1) * d_model * d_model
    attention_ops_no_cache += n_heads * (t+1) * (t+1) * (d_model // n_heads)
no_cache_time = (time.time() - start) * 1000

# Verify outputs match
cached_final = np.concatenate(cached_outputs, axis=1)
no_cache_final = np.concatenate(no_cache_outputs, axis=1)

print(f"Results match: {np.allclose(cached_final, no_cache_final, atol=1e-6)}")
print()
print(f"With KV-cache:    {cached_time:.2f} ms")
print(f"Without KV-cache: {no_cache_time:.2f} ms")
print(f"Speedup: {no_cache_time/cached_time:.1f}x")
print()
print(f"Projection operations - Cached: {projection_ops_cached:>12,} | No cache: {projection_ops_no_cache:>12,}")
print(f"  Savings: {1 - projection_ops_cached/projection_ops_no_cache:.1%}")
print()
print(f"Attention operations  - Cached: {attention_ops_cached:>12,} | No cache: {attention_ops_no_cache:>12,}")
print(f"  Savings: {1 - attention_ops_cached/attention_ops_no_cache:.1%}")
print()
print(f"KV-cache size at end: {model_cached.k_cache.shape}")
print(f"  = {model_cached.k_cache.size + model_cached.v_cache.size} float values stored")
